rules.text: Only calendars with access_role of 'writer' or 'owner' permit event creation, modification, or deletion.
Creating or updating an event cannot overlap with an existing confirmed event for any required attendee or on the target calendar.
Updating an event requires specifying an expected_version that matches the current event version in the database to prevent concurrent write conflicts.
Minimum buffer time in minutes required between scheduled events.
Scheduling window constraints defining minimum notice required and maximum horizon days into the future.
Attendee domain allowlist restriction for meeting invites (* permits any domain).
Whether creating, updating, or deleting calendar events strictly requires an approved approval_id.
The agent must present event time, timezone, and attendees and obtain explicit user approval before executing any creation, update, or deletion.
The agent must not claim a slot is reserved based only on an availability suggestion and must gracefully handle slot conflict errors if a race occurs.
The agent must ask for clarification when a requested time falls on an ambiguous daylight-saving transition boundary before creating an event.
When a mutation encounters a timeout or ambiguous network error, the agent must inspect event state using get_event instead of blindly creating duplicate events.
The agent must preserve original event details without modifying or deleting them if a reschedule request fails or encounters an unresolved conflict.
When managing recurring events, the agent must distinguish between deleting or modifying a single occurrence versus the entire recurring series.
